narrative: A young man from Aleppo fled the war in Syria and, in June 2015, became part of the largest human migration since the Second World War. On the way to Europe he survived a dangerous sea crossing to Greece, then braved beatings by police in Macedonia and persisted through countless miles on foot and nights exposed to the elements before reaching Germany. He was granted asylum and settled in Berlin, later attending a small liberal-arts university on a scholarship for students from crisis areas. His mother and sister remained in Aleppo, and two years after his own arrival he spent roughly $4,000, raised partly with help from a stranger he met through his story, to pay a smuggler to bring them out; after a nerve-wracking stretch when the intermediary was taken by an armed group and his family went out of contact at the border, he received word that they had reached Turkey safely.
